newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HEARTS SEND HIBS INTO RELEGATION ZONE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HEARTS SEND HIBS INTO RELEGATION ZONE.

text.p: Hibernian are in real relegation trouble after a 1-0 defeat at Edinburgh rival Hearts left them second-from-bottom in the Scottish premier division on Saturday.
Kilmarnock leapt towards safety with a vital 1-0 success over fellow strugglers Motherwell while Raith look dead and buried after going down 1-0 at home to Dunfermline.
Dundee United, seemingly secure in third place, extended their unbeaten run to 16 games with a 1-1 draw at Aberdeen.
Leaders Rangers visit second-placed Celtic on Sunday.
At Tynecastle, Hearts sent their neighbours into the relegation zone with a goal eight minutes from time.
Neil McCann scored it following a cross by former Everton full back Neil Pointon.
It should have been two soon after when Steve Fulton missed when clean through but it proved immaterial.
Aberdeen went ahead with a Dean Windass penalty after Mark Perry had fouled Scott Booth in the first half and were good value for their lead.
But United, still on a high from Wednesday's 2-0 victory at Rangers, came back well after the break and deservedly equalised through Kjell Olofsson 20 minutes from time.
In the relegation duel at Rugby Park, Paul Wright's vital strike 13 minutes from time moved Kilmarnock up to seventh place and left Motherwell eighth.
A goal by Dunfermline's Andy Smith settled the Fife derby against Raith in favour of the visitors on a very heavy Stark's Park pitch.

East Fife became the first team in Britain to be officially relegated after Saturday's 4-1 division one defeat at Stirling. They have managed just one win in 29 attempts and have mustered only 10 points.
